title: Brucie Smash: No Banner only HULK Drops 177.86 and Turns Week 1 Into a Hostile Takeover
dek: Ramon's crew posts the biggest opening number in league history, Randy's Bears QB goes nuclear, Zoe wins her debut, and Sonny opens his title defense by edging the villain.
body: One year ago, Ramon got shown the door for inactivity. This Sunday, No Banner only HULK walked back in and put up 177.86 points, flattening Mekhi's Dawgs by 79.5 and beating Brucie's own 2024 opener of 166.58. Josh Allen threw in 35.66 for his favorite Bills fan, Kenneth Walker III ran for 32.6, and D'Andre Swift added 31.9, which means a Chicago-born turncoat rode a Bears running back to the top of a league full of Bears fans. The only blemish was the Texans D/ST at minus-4, and when your defense loses you points and you still win by nearly 80, the rest of the league has a problem. HULK's title odds jumped from 11% to 47%, and somewhere a group chat is quietly seething.

Kai never had a chance, and he helped the other guy a little. Ja'Marr Chase managed 2.2 points against a 16.44 projection, while Christian Watson sat on the Dawgs' bench and racked up 29.7. Swap those two and Mekhi still loses, but it would have looked like a football game instead of a hostage video. For the league's sharpest football mind, who drafted from overseas this year, the title odds went from a co-league-high 17% to 1% in one afternoon. The waiver wire is going to get a workout this week.

Randy had the other big afternoon, and it came from the most Randy source imaginable. Caleb Williams threw for 37.26 points, the best performance of the week, on a 16.39 projection, and Derrick Henry chipped in 34.8 as The fumblers crushed Counting or not Counting GV 146.16 to 75.96. Not every Bears guy cooperated: Colston Loveland posted a perfectly round zero. Randy jumped from 15% to 28% title odds, and he gets to tell everyone his quarterback is the best in the league, at least until next Sunday.

JMoney, the man who came for the numbers, will not enjoy these numbers. Ashton Jeanty scored 29.7 from the Counting or not Counting GV bench, nearly 40% of Jordan's entire team total, and the 75.96 was the lowest score of the week by more than 22 points. That leaves Jordan with 3% playoff odds and a title-odds reading of 0%, which is at least a number he can calculate easily. It's one week, but the lineup page needs a long look.

Zoe's fantasy career is 1-0, and she did it with one hand tied behind her back. Ghostu-Spider SZN beat Kaushal's Habibsters 129.56 to 108.6 as a slight underdog, and that was with David Montgomery's 27.4 stuck on the bench. Z Squared sits third in points and holds steady at 13% title odds with 76% playoff odds, the kind of debut that makes veterans nervous. Habibi, meanwhile, watched his title odds crater from 17% to 3% and responded by swapping the Browns D/ST for the Jaguars D/ST, the fantasy equivalent of changing the oil after the engine fell out.

The defending champ opened his title defense as a 46% underdog and escaped. Sonny's The Horse is Hea held off Alan's Team Pillbert 106.42 to 102.1, despite Jahmyr Gibbs dropping 31.1 for the villain. Philliberto came within four points of spoiling the champion's banner week and will spend all week explaining how close he came. Strangely, the computer was not impressed with Sonny's win: his title odds fell from 9% to 4%. He's already tinkering, dropping T.J. Hockenson for Mark Andrews at tight end.

Week 2 has a heavyweight undercard. No Banner only HULK hosts the rookie in Ramon vs Zoe, a matchup of unbeatens where Zilgit gets the first crack at the monster. Mekhi tries to dig out against Randy, Jordan looks for redemption against the champion, and Alan and Kaushal meet in a battle of 0-1 teams that both expected better. Thirteen weeks remain, but Brucie already has the league exactly where he likes it: annoyed and looking up at him.

social.author: HULK Nation
social.text: 177.86. Kicked out in 2025, kicking down doors in 2026. Somebody hand Ramon a banner already.

social.author: Bears Bar Barry
social.text: Caleb Williams 37 points, D'Andre Swift 31.9 points. Great week for the Bears. Terrible week to realize one of them plays for a Bills fan.

social.author: Fantasy Coroner
social.text: Cause of death for the Dawgs: Ja'Marr Chase, 2.2 points. Contributing factor: Christian Watson, 29.7 points, bench. Ruled a tragedy.

social.author: Cheesehead Collective
social.text: Zoe wins her first ever fantasy game with Montgomery's 27 on the bench. Imagine when she starts the right guys. Wisconsin is rising.

social.author: The Spreadsheet Guy
social.text: Counting or not Counting GV left 29.7 on the bench and scored 75.96. JMoney, the formula is: start the guy who scores.

social.author: Waiver Wire Whisperer
social.text: Habibsters lose by 21 and the fix is... a defense swap. Bold. Jaguars D/ST, the Habibi era starts now, apparently.

social.author: Villain Watch
social.text: Philly lost by 4.32 to the champ. Gibbs gave him 31. The bad guy will be back, and he will be insufferable about the margin.

social.author: BFL Insider
social.text: Sources say The Horse is Hea won and lost title odds in the same day. Commissioner reportedly reviewing the algorithm. Totally normal.

bios.1: The defending champ survived Alan by 4.32 as an underdog to start 1-0. The odds still dipped to 4%, so Sonny is already tinkering, adding Mark Andrews for T.J. Hockenson.
bios.2: Randy's squad hung 146.16 on Jordan behind Caleb Williams' week-best 37.26 and Derrick Henry's 34.8. Title odds nearly doubled to 28%, zero from Colston Loveland notwithstanding. A clear No. 2 after one week.
bios.3: Jordan's 75.96 was the week's low score, and Ashton Jeanty's 29.7 on the bench made it sting. Playoff odds sit at 3%. A date with the defending champion is next.
bios.4: Alan got 31.1 from Jahmyr Gibbs and still fell 4.32 short of the champion. At 0-1 with 32% playoff odds, the villain is down but nowhere near out. Next up: Kaushal.
bios.5: Mekhi ran into the 177-point buzzsaw while Ja'Marr Chase scored 2.2 and Christian Watson's 29.7 sat on the bench. Title odds fell from 17% to 1%. The waiver king has some work to do, starting with Randy.
bios.6: Kaushal opened with 108.6 points and a loss to the rookie, and his title odds tumbled from 17% to 3%. The only move so far is a defense swap to the Jaguars. Plenty of season left for the two-time champ to find his gear.
bios.7: Ramon opened with 177.86 points, a league-record opener powered by Josh Allen, Kenneth Walker III and D'Andre Swift. Title odds rocketed to 47% even with the Texans D/ST going negative. The favorite, and everyone knows it.
bios.8: Zoe won her fantasy debut 129.56 to 108.6 over a two-time champ, with 27.4 points sitting on her bench. Playoff odds stand at 76%. The rookie looks like a contender, and HULK is up next.
